case.question: I fish for salmon from a boat. For this week, how good do you expect boat fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation
- Fish from a boat out of **Grand Haven**. I'd rate it **1 of 4** this week, the best of the four but still slow.
- Troll 100 to 200 ft of water, near the pierheads and in the channel, with lines running about 75 to 120 ft down.
- Start with glow J-plugs or white flasher flies, or glow spoons. Those are the lures the recent boat reports named.
- Expect the other three ports to be about as slow. I'd rate South Haven 1, St. Joseph 0 to 1, and Muskegon 1 with low confidence.

## Why
- The newest boat reports at all four ports were slow or below average, so none of them looks good right now (Grand Haven, South Haven, and St. Joseph, 2023-09-27).
- Grand Haven had the only excellent boat results this season, with glow J-plugs and white flashers in the channel and at the pierheads (Grand Haven, 2023-09-13), so it has the best recent record.
- I'd expect the lines to need to be deep, because the fish were 75 to 120 ft down in 120 to 200 ft of water in the latest Grand Haven report (Grand Haven, 2023-09-27).
- Muskegon's latest boat result is from 2023-09-06, almost four weeks old, so I can't judge it well.

## Evidence
**Recent reports**
- Grand Haven, 2023-09-27: boat, 120 to 200 ft water, fish 75 to 120 ft down, quality 0 (slow). "A few immature salmon were caught 75 to 120 feet down in 120 to 200 feet of water." Glow spoons and white paddle/flies "worked well" (mode not stated, so treat as unclear).
- South Haven, 2023-09-27: boat, about 110 ft of water, quality 0 (slow). "There were a few fish caught in around 110 feet of water."
- St. Joseph, 2023-09-27: boat, 100+ ft of water, quality 0 (slow). "A few fish caught in well past 100 feet of water, but overall, it was slow."
- Muskegon: boat report on 2023-09-06 only, quality 1, chrome J-plugs in the channel.
- Grand Haven, 2023-09-13: boat, quality 4 for both Chinook and coho, glow J-plugs and white flashers, "in the channel and in front of the pierheads."
- Grand Haven, 2023-09-20: boat, 100 to 200 ft of water, fish 65 to 110 ft down, big white paddles with white or green flies "worked well" (quality not rated).

**Past seasons (history, not current)**
- In late September 2022, South Haven boats did best in 120+ ft of water on spoons (quality 3, 2022-09-28).
- In early October 2022, St. Joseph boats did best around 120 ft on spoons (quality 2, 2022-10-05).
- Similar-temperature weeks in past seasons (about 62 to 70 F) mostly reported slow to average boat fishing, so I'd expect this to stay a slow-to-average week.

**Conditions now**
- Live conditions weren't available. The tool returned a summary of the week before 2023-10-03 instead, so I'm treating it as a guide only.
- Measured buoy surface water was about 64 to 67 F across the four ports, and the buoys showed little change over the week.
- Upwelling-favoring wind (north to east, 8+ mph) totaled about 34 to 41 h at Grand Haven and Muskegon, and 16 to 19 h at St. Joseph and South Haven. None of the four ports had any of it in the last 3 days.
- General guidance (NY DEC): Chinook and coho prefer 52 to 58 F. At 64 to 67 F, the fish are likely deeper and more spread out, which fits the deep-water reports.

## Caveats
- The newest boat report is from 2023-09-27, about a week old. Conditions can change quickly this time of year.
- The water and wind figures are a summary for the week before 2023-10-03, not a live reading or a forecast. I couldn't check this weekend's wind, so check the marine forecast before you go out.
- The Grand Haven and Muskegon wind hours came from the same week, and none of the four ports showed upwelling in the last 3 days.
- Muskegon has little recent boat data, and the South Haven and St. Joseph ratings are based on one slow report each.
